Construction of Footpaths in Hill and Rural Areas  The construction of footpaths in hill and rural areas is very important for improving daily life, safety, and connectivity of villages. In many hilly regions, roads are limited and people mostly travel on foot to reach schools, farms, markets, water sources, and health centres. Proper footpaths help villagers move safely and easily, especially during rainy seasons when the terrain becomes slippery and dangerous.

Construction of waiting or bus sheds will provide Significant practical benefits in rural hilly village especially in region like Nagaland India where roads are winding, public transport is infrequent, weather is unpredictable and villages are often remote benefits protection from harsh weather, shelter from rain, wind extreme heat. this waiting shed will be as multipurpose use and low cost community asset.

This project focuses on the preservation of the historic Kalyana Mantapa within the Vijaya Vittala Temple complex. Persistent water seepage from the roof threatens its structural integrity and exquisite stone carvings. The scope involves urgent retrofitting, roof repair, and architectural conservation. Under MPLADS guidelines, I recommend an administrative sanction of Rs. 50 Lakhs for this work, with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) serving as the implementing agency.

This project focuses on the 270m stretch of the North Bazar at Virupaksha Temple. The stone mantapas suffer from severe weathering and structural decay. The scope includes structural inventory, propping columns, architectural stabilization, and debris removal to adaptively reuse the spaces for community use. Under MPLADS, I recommend an allocation of Rs. 4.40 Crores for FY 2026-2027. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) will act as the implementing agency.
